prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. Produce exactly ONE finished single flat opaque landscape 16:9 SNS poster for a weekend houseplant market, with the complete typography and painting generated together. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

The supplied image is my newly authored planning diagram for actual copy anatomy, meaningful line groups, relative type hierarchy and substantive image geometry. It is not client artwork, a final style, or fixed coordinates. Interpret its pot/canopy placeholders into the real overhead painted scene described here. Its 1600×900 canvas is a neutral planning guide, not a required output pixel size. Do not reproduce its gray-green blobs or passive gray field. Reference the mature open Korean counters and stable sans proportions without claiming a particular font file is applied.

Whole design: looking down closely into a lively gathering of living planted pots. A dominant two-line Korean serif Title at upper left occupies generous space above a broad low-left canopy. Unequal overhead pot circles and asymmetrical real leaves create a continuous irregular gathering from high middle down through an open branching middle plant to a large lower-left plant. A smaller third pot at lower middle links the gathering; their visible soil, stems, pot rims and attached shadows make every canopy belong to a living pot. This is the pleasure of comparing different houseplants and tending them in window light. Use a leafy mature jade/rubber-like plant high in the middle, an airy branching canopy immediately below, and broad richly painted calathea-like leaves expanding under the Title and cropping naturally at the lower-left edge. Keep a legible crescent of the broad plant's rim and its stem-to-soil attachment. Leaves vary in size, angle, age, light and vein treatment. They overlap at different living scales. Do not turn this into one giant right tree, an upright forest silhouette, isolated sticker icons, or an independent bottom picture strip.

Expressive opaque gouache masses, controlled dry-brush edges, selective drawn leaf veins and actual paint layering. Deep plum for the heaviest pot/shadow and typography accents, sap green with olive and yellow-green foliage, ochre ceramic rim light, creamy painted light. Window illumination is selective and coherent, with soft attached diagonal shadows grounding the pots on one shared painted support. Make the foliage and irregular rim rhythm substantively organize the space between the left title and the right reading route. Broad light clearances for text may remain, but they must belong to this plant gathering's rhythm and light, without boxed information panels or a hard vertical color split. There are no people, plant labels, tags or printed objects.

Typography and route: upper-left smaller market eyebrow, then the Korean Title as the unmistakable primary typographic anchor. Break that Title after its first two words into two generous lines, as in the guide. Give it much greater body and optical weight than all prose, Latin, date or invitation: mature Korean serif, open interior spaces, controlled contrast, substantial strokes, consistent syllable proportions. A quieter Latin companion follows immediately below the Title. One harmonious medium sans reading system supplies eyebrow, secondary subtitle, prose, numerals and useful details; the subtitle has a modest semibold distinction. The serif Title and stable sans share mature proportions and coherent weight. No distorted, playful, clay, calligraphic or decorative body lettering.

Across the central pot-rim rhythm, begin the right continuous reading route with the secondary promise subtitle. Below it set the complete explanation as five meaningful left-aligned lines, breaking at the word spaces after '키운', after the first period, after the comma and after '맞는'. Keep those five lines together, generous medium body, about 17px optical body at a 720px-wide view, orderly line spacing. The right text start remains constant. Directly below its last line, a moderate group gap leads into date, hours and venue; access and care follow locally, then invitation and URL. All these practical lines are comfortably readable at 720px wide, similar medium sans with clear word spaces. Do not move schedule back to the left or distribute lines into remote corners. Reserve adequate clearance so no rim, stem, divider, shadow or vein touches a glyph. No decorative rules, arrows, bullets, pipes, headings or numbers beyond the literal copy.

Print only the following exact copy, each entry once. Preserve every Korean/Latin character, letter case, meaningful word space, number and punctuation. Preserve the true en dash in both ranges, exact middle dots, comma, periods, ampersand and URL slash. No added print, logo, watermark, QR, slogan, caption, style name or label. This copy list supplies content; its role labels and quote marks are instructions only, not printing:
Market eyebrow: "성수 주말 식물 마켓"
Primary Korean Title: "집 안의 작은 숲"
Latin companion: "LEAVES & LIVING"
Right secondary subtitle: "초록을 고르고, 일상을 가꿉니다."
Five-line continuous explanation: "작은 화분부터 오래 키운 나무까지 만납니다. 재배자의 이야기를 듣고, 우리 집의 빛과 생활에 맞는 식물을 골라보세요."
Date: "2027.06.12–06.13"
Hours: "토·일 11:00–19:00"
Venue: "성수 온실마당"
Access: "입장 무료 · 분갈이 시연"
Care: "식물 구매 시 관리 안내 제공"
Invitation: "편하게 들러 천천히 둘러보세요."
URL: "leaves.example/market"

Flat precise typesetting, consistent baselines and optical language scales; no painting texture or perspective applied to small text. Use visibly extended en dashes, distinguish middle dots from periods, and provide clean colon shapes. Finish the gouache image with intentional dry edges and connected pots/branches/shadows, avoiding arbitrary decorative grain or shapeless soft blobs.

Exclude the passive solid/near-solid/split-field gothic headline/date/information template with subordinate tiny images, a texture or font substitution, or empty-room dressing. Merely substituting a serif title into that template is also excluded. This poster's overhead plant gathering and overlapping rim/canopy geometry must shape its whole spatial organization. No mockup, frame, contact sheet, comparison panel, collage of multiple posters or extra image.
